images.title: Heights in another Grade 5 section
images.purpose: Give the dot plots the question asks students to read: the whole class, the boys and the girls of another Grade 5 section, each with its mean and median lines.
images.composition: Three dot plots stacked vertically, each on a scale from 125 to 155 cm, each with a solid mean line, a dashed median line and a small key to its right.
exact_structure: Top plot labelled Whole class: grey (#6B7280) dots spread from about 127 to 158 cm, crowded between 140 and 150; a solid vertical line at 141.21 and a dashed vertical line at 142.5.
Middle plot labelled Boys: teal (#0072B2) dots spread from about 130 to 148 cm, most of them stacked between 142 and 146; a solid line at 142.05 and a dashed line at 143.
Bottom plot labelled Girls: vermilion (#D55E00) dots spread from about 126 to 158 cm, more evenly spread out with small stacks near 135 and 140; a solid line at 140.14 and a dashed line at 140.
Every plot has numbered ticks at 125, 130, 135, 140, 145, 150 and 155.
To the right of each plot a key reads the mean beside a short solid line and the median beside a short dashed line.
rejection: the mean and median lines drawn in the same style
means or medians that differ from the labels
images.takeaway: In this section the boys' heights crowd together and sit a little higher; the girls' heights are spread more widely.
images.description: Three dot plots of heights for a whole class, its boys and its girls, each with its mean and median marked.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask students to compare the spread of the boys' and girls' dots, not only the two means.

images.title: Empty dot plot for newborn weights
images.purpose: Give students the empty scale on which to mark the newborn weights for boys and girls.
images.composition: One wide empty grid with a number line below it.
exact_structure: A light grey grid of 3 horizontal rows and 9 columns above a number line.
The number line runs from 0 to 4.5 with numbered ticks at 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4 and 4.5.
No dots are drawn; the grid is empty for students to fill.
A small key in the top right: a teal (#0072B2) dot labelled Boys and an amber (#E69F00) dot labelled Girls.
rejection: a scale that does not go up in steps of 0.5
images.takeaway: Each weight becomes one dot above its value, so boys and girls can be compared at a glance.
images.description: An empty grid over a number line from 0 to 4.5 kg with a key for boys and girls.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Students mark the twelve weights themselves; do not show any dots.

images.title: Empty dot plot for palm tree heights
images.purpose: Give students the empty scale on which to mark the 29 palm tree heights and then the mean and median.
images.composition: One wide empty grid with a number line below it.
exact_structure: A light grey grid of 4 horizontal rows above a number line.
The number line runs from 0 to 80 with numbered ticks at every 5: 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, 65, 70, 75 and 80, and small unnumbered ticks at every whole number.
No dots and no mean or median lines are drawn; the grid is empty for students to fill.
The caption under the line reads Height (in feet).
rejection: a mean or median line already drawn
images.takeaway: Each tree height becomes one dot; repeated heights stack, which shows where the heights crowd.
images.description: An empty dot plot grid over a number line from 0 to 80 feet.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Students mark the heights themselves; do not show any dots.

images.title: A zero counts, a blank does not
images.purpose: Show that a real zero is a data value and stays in, while a missing entry is left out of the count.
images.composition: One row of six equal boxes across the middle of the frame, with one short result line centred below it.
exact_structure: Exactly 6 square boxes in one row, evenly spaced, teal #0072B2 outlines.
The boxes hold, left to right: 3, 0, 5, no entry, 4, 0.
The two boxes holding 0 are filled light green #009E73 to show they are kept as values.
The no entry box is grey #6B7280 with a single grey diagonal line through it, struck out.
Below the row, one line in dark text: Count 5 values, mean = 12 ÷ 5 = 2.4.
Arithmetic check for the reviewer only, NOT drawn in the frame: 3 + 0 + 5 + 4 + 0 = 12, and 12 ÷ 5 = 2.4.
rejection: either 0 box struck out or greyed
the no entry box not struck out
a divisor other than 5 or a mean other than 2.4
images.takeaway: Zeros are values and are counted; a missing entry is left out before dividing.
images.description: Six boxes reading 3, 0, 5, no entry, 4, 0; the blank is struck out and the caption shows the mean 12 ÷ 5 = 2.4.
images.context: Shown on the practice concept before the zero-or-blank questions.
images.teaching_notes: Ask which boxes go into the count before reading the caption.

image_decisions.why: Three questions in this set depend on a figure: dot plots to read, and two empty scales to fill.
